name: core-ultra-layout-v2
note: The design factors a design condition is made of, the values the reference layout engine draws for each, and the layout families: each family is one named combination of factor values, chosen as a whole. The scene model is given the factor values, never a family's name. Navigation position is where the toolbar's elements sit: a bar across the top, a rail down the left side or a bar across the bottom. Panel arrangement is where the document list sits beside the editor: a column on the left, a column on the right, or a grid of rows across the top. Density scales the visual preset's heights and spacing scales its distances, each by one factor for every token of the group (`preset` leaves them as the preset states them). Notification location is where along the lower edge of the area the navigation leaves free the notification lies. The families are preferences, not rules: the engine draws any combination of these values, every value is used by at least two families, and none is the correct one. `out_of_scope` lists the variation the generator does not produce. A changed layout is a new version of this file, never an edit to this one once a dataset has been generated from it.

top-bar-list-left.title: Top bar, list left
top-bar-list-left.summary: The toolbar across the top, the document list on the left, the editor filling the rest and the notification over the lower right corner.

top-bar-list-right.title: Top bar, list right
top-bar-list-right.summary: The toolbar across the top, the editor on the left and the document list on the right, taller elements and wider distances, the notification at the middle of the lower edge.

top-bar-list-top.title: Top bar, list across the top
top-bar-list-top.summary: The toolbar across the top, the documents as a grid of rows under it and the editor below, shorter elements and closer distances, the notification over the lower right corner.

left-rail-list-left.title: Left rail, list left
left-rail-list-left.summary: The toolbar's elements stacked in a rail down the left side, the document list beside it and the editor filling the rest, shorter elements, the notification over the lower left corner, under the list.

left-rail-list-right.title: Left rail, list right
left-rail-list-right.summary: The toolbar's elements stacked in a rail down the left side, the editor beside it and the document list on the right, closer distances, the notification at the middle of the lower edge.

left-rail-list-top.title: Left rail, list across the top
left-rail-list-top.summary: The toolbar's elements stacked in a rail down the left side, the documents as a grid of rows across the top and the editor below, taller elements and wider distances, the notification over the lower right corner.

bottom-bar-list-left.title: Bottom bar, list left
bottom-bar-list-left.summary: The toolbar across the bottom, the document list on the left and the editor filling the rest above it, taller elements, the notification over the lower left corner, under the list.

bottom-bar-list-right.title: Bottom bar, list right
bottom-bar-list-right.summary: The toolbar across the bottom, the editor on the left and the document list on the right above it, shorter elements and closer distances, the notification at the middle of the lower edge.

out_of_scope: Scrolling. Nothing scrolls, so a workspace holds at most 32 bound elements (21 list rows) and only as many rows and lines as its viewport shows.
Text that wraps, is cut short or ends in an ellipsis. Every text is one line (a document body, one line per line feed) and must fit its box as it is.
Right-to-left and vertical text, and any character the Inter font has no glyph for (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, emoji).
More than one font family, and italic or condensed styles. Presets differ in type size and weight only.

Alignment as a factor of its own. Alignment changes only as a consequence of navigation position, panel arrangement and notification location; no family right-aligns or centres the text of rows, fields or labels.
Style values randomised one by one. A design is a whole visual preset and a whole layout family; no token is drawn independently of the rest of its set.
Arrangements that change with the viewport. The arrangement comes from the design condition alone; a narrow viewport never folds the list away or moves the navigation.
Navigation on the right, hidden or collapsed navigation, tabs, menus, icons and images. The toolbar always holds the same six bound elements, as text.
A notification along the upper edge. There it lies over the title field or the first rows of the list, which the validators reject.
More than two panels, nested or floating panels, dialogs, and more than one notification at a time.
Element states beyond default, hover, pressed, focused and disabled, more than one pointed element at a time, selection and drag.
Workspaces other than the document workspace, and document lists the scripted sessions do not reach (the longest scripted list has nine documents).
Motion. A record is one still frame.
